community_posts.title: ⚠️ How to check if your medicine is genuine - Doctor's guide
community_posts.body:
As a doctor, I see patients worried about fake medicines. Here are simple checks:

1. Check the batch number on the strip matches the box
2. Look for the manufacturer's hologram (if applicable)
3. Verify expiry date - never take expired medicines
4. Check MRP - if price seems too low from a regular pharmacy, be cautious
5. Use apps like MedSathi to scan and verify
6. Buy from licensed pharmacies only
7. Check the CDSCO website for any recalls

Remember: Generic medicines are NOT fake. They contain the same active ingredient. Jan Aushadhi medicines are government-quality tested.

community_posts.title: Understanding your blood pressure medicines 💊
community_posts.body:
Common BP medicines explained simply:

🔵 Amlodipine (Amlong/Amlip) - Calcium channel blocker, relaxes blood vessels
🔵 Telmisartan (Telma/Telmikind) - ARB, blocks hormone that narrows vessels
🔵 Atenolol (Aten/Tenormin) - Beta blocker, slows heart rate
🔵 Losartan (Losacar/Repace) - ARB, similar to Telmisartan

All available as Jan Aushadhi generics at 60-80% less cost!

IMPORTANT: Never stop BP medicine suddenly. Always consult your doctor before any changes.

community_posts.title: 🏥 Doctor's tip: Never do these 5 things with antibiotics
community_posts.body:
As a practicing physician, here are 5 common antibiotic mistakes I see daily:

1️⃣ NEVER stop antibiotics early because you feel better — complete the full course
2️⃣ NEVER share antibiotics with family members — different infections need different treatments
3️⃣ NEVER take antibiotics for viral infections (cold, flu) — they don't work
4️⃣ NEVER skip doses — take at regular intervals as prescribed
5️⃣ NEVER self-prescribe antibiotics from pharmacy — always get a prescription

Antibiotic resistance is a serious problem in India. Misuse of antibiotics makes them less effective over time. This affects ALL of us.

Share this widely! 🙏
